To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the push‐pull local exhaust venting is an effective mitigation measure to control workers' exposure to VOCs in the printing plant.

(1) short‐term exposure to VOC‐emitting intermittent procedures is the main cause of health risks; (2) push‐pull LEVs are effective in reducing the exposure; and (3) the LEV air flow threshold exists and is less sensitive to higher air flows.

the occupational exposure to VOCs was mainly due to intermittent VOC‐emission procedures, and that the push‐pull local exhaust system was an effective mitigation measure for such intermittent emission procedures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of VOCs in offset lithographic printers and their mitigation by push‐pull LEVs.
the IAQ in printing plants and the development of effective control measures to protect workers from VOCs.
the development of an IAQ assessment methodology and the identification of an effective LEV system for the mitigation of VOC emissions in offset lithographic print shops.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the push‐pull ventilation is effective in reducing the worker's exposure when it is properly designed, installed, and operated.
the use of push‐pull LEVs can reduce the workers' short‐term exposure to VOCs by 50% or more.
the IAQ in printing plants is generally acceptable and there is no need to implement any control measure for the background VOCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IAQ of a print shop is not a major concern, but a print worker is at risk of being overexposed to VOCs during intermittent tasks.
the push‐pull local exhaust is a cost‐effective mitigation measure for VOCs in printing plants and the threshold LEV air‐flow rate should be determined by the CFD analysis.

the IAQ assessment in the printing plant should be conducted in a holistic manner, considering both long‐ and short‐term exposure to VOCs, and the push‐push LEV should be operated above the threshold air flow rate for the best performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the push‐pull local exhaust system should be designed to provide a high air flow rate for the LEV hood to ensure that it is able to overcome the general ventilation and become the dominating driving source for the local flow pattern.
push‐pull LEVs are effective in reducing workers’ exposure to high levels of VOCs during intermittent tasks.
the push‐pull local exhaust system should be designed with sufficient air flow rates to provide adequate protection to workers.
